files.rightContent:
# Bygone: every view in context

Screenshot walkthrough for Bygone 0.11.1. Synthetic code and review data.

## Two files, one visual language

Blue ribbons connect changed regions; green marks additions. Local files can be edited. Use this for concrete before/after questions.

![Two files, one visual language](images/01-two-files.png)

Entry: `bygone before.js after.js`



## More than two versions

Add versions to see an evolution in one view. Fit changes how many panes are visible; the selected adjacent pair determines the active comparison.

![More than two versions](images/02-many-panels.png)

Entry: `bygone --diff v1.js v2.js v3.js v4.js v5.js`



## Start with directory differences

Compare trees, then drill into a changed path. This is a comparison inventory, not a merge tool.

![Start with directory differences](images/03-directories.png)

Entry: `bygone before/ after/`



## Search across the comparison

Find the same idea across panes, then inspect each result in its source context. Replacement is limited to writable sources.

![Search across the comparison](images/04-search.png)

Entry: `Cmd/Ctrl+F • Search Comparison • Search in Files`



## Start without a file

Use an untitled editable comparison for snippets. It has no Git provenance until you save or explicitly compare real sources.

![Start without a file](images/08-blank-editor.png)

Entry: `bygone --diff`



## Browse a repository through time

Files and commits provide two routes into history. Committed snapshots remain read-only.

![Browse a repository through time](images/05-repository-history.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo --history .`



## Follow one file through commits

Use a path when the question is how one file evolved. The history navigator selects concrete revisions.

![Follow one file through commits](images/06-file-history.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo release.js`



## Orient before reading every file

Branch review starts from the committed change against its merge base. The overview offers a reading order; dirty work is separate.

![Orient before reading every file](images/07-branch-review.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo review feature --base main`



## Name the endpoints explicitly

Compare commits and work states. HEAD and INDEX are read-only; WORKTREE can be writable. These labels are different kinds of evidence.

![Name the endpoints explicitly](images/09-git-snapshots.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo --git-diff HEAD~2 HEAD WORKTREE`



## One file, three saved states

HEAD: stable · Index: preview · Saved file: canary The same file appears under Staged Changes and Changes. These are two different comparisons.

![One file, three saved states](images/09a-scm-setup.png)

Entry: `Open Source Control with release.js selected.`



## Inspect what would be committed

Before: Source Control shows staged and unstaged work. Bygone compares HEAD stable → Index preview. Both sides are read-only; canary is excluded.

![Inspect what would be committed](images/11-scm-staged.png)

Entry: `Staged Changes → release.js → Open Staged Changes in Bygone.`



## Inspect what remains unstaged

Before: the staged comparison was stable → preview. The baseline is now Index preview; the writable side is the saved document canary.

![Inspect what remains unstaged](images/13-scm-working.png)

Entry: `Changes → release.js → Open Working Changes in Bygone.`



## Choose active-editor following

Before: release.js is saved as canary; index remains preview. The command is selected here. Press Enter to follow the active local document.

![Choose active-editor following](images/10a-follow-command.png)

Entry: `Focus release.js. Open the Command Palette and choose Bygone: Follow Active Editor.`



## See unsaved text in Bygone

Before: working document canary. Both views now show nightly. The dirty dot and Unsaved buffer label distinguish it from the saved file.

![See unsaved text in Bygone](images/10-follow-dirty.png)

Entry: `In the regular editor, replace canary with nightly. Leave the file unsaved.`



## Pin, then actually navigate away

Before: Bygone was following release.js. The native pane shows policy.js; pinned Bygone still shows release.js. Navigation did not replace it.

![Pin, then actually navigate away](images/14-pinned.png)

Entry: `Click Pin in Bygone. Open policy.js in the regular VS Code pane.`



## Return to the intended comparison

Before: release.js was pinned while policy.js was active. The active comparison is Index preview → unsaved nightly. Keep these endpoints while focusing a symbol.

![Return to the intended comparison](images/14b-resume-working.png)

Entry: `Source Control → Changes → release.js → Open Working Changes in Bygone.`



## Choose a symbol from the cursor

Before: the comparison contains the whole file. The selected command uses VS Code’s current cursor or selection. Press Enter to focus this declaration.

![Choose a symbol from the cursor](images/15a-symbol-command.png)

Entry: `Place the cursor inside planRelease. Choose Bygone: Compare Symbol in Bygone.`



## Narrow the view, preserve the comparison

Before: whole-file Index preview → working nightly. Both panes now contain planRelease. The same baseline and live document remain selected.

![Narrow the view, preserve the comparison](images/15-symbol-slice.png)

Entry: `Run Compare Symbol in Bygone from inside planRelease.`



## Edit in Bygone; see it in VS Code

Before: native editor and Bygone both showed nightly. Both now show dev. The index pane still shows preview; this is one shared, unsaved document.

![Edit in Bygone; see it in VS Code](images/16-synced-edit.png)

Entry: `In Bygone’s right-hand symbol pane, replace nightly with dev.`



## Undo once, update both views

Before: the previous edit changed nightly → dev. The regular editor and Bygone both return to nightly. The file is still unsaved.

![Undo once, update both views](images/17-shared-undo.png)

Entry: `Click Undo in Bygone.`



## Save the document, keep the index

Before: working document nightly was dirty; index was preview. Saved buffer replaces Unsaved buffer, and the dirty dot clears. The index remains preview.

![Save the document, keep the index](images/18-save-no-stage.png)

Entry: `Click Save in Bygone.`



## Open a saved review

Before: you were editing a live working document. The review displays its pinned Git identities and cited source references. It is a separate artifact.

![Open a saved review](images/19-evidence-review.png)

Entry: `Run Bygone: Open Evidence Review and select review.json for this repository.`



## Read the exact cited file diff

Before: the review listed a source citation. Bygone opens the review’s committed comparison. Your working nightly text is not substituted into it.

![Read the exact cited file diff](images/21-pinned-diff.png)

Entry: `In Evidence Review, choose Pinned file diff for planRelease.`



## Open a live counterpart for editing

Before: you were inspecting an immutable committed diff. A separate working view opens with Return to Evidence Review available. The live value is nightly.

![Open a live counterpart for editing](images/22-evidence-repair.png)

Entry: `Return to Evidence Review. Choose Edit working counterpart for the same reference.`



## Make a real working edit

Before: the live counterpart showed nightly. The regular document now contains candidate. The captured review still refers to its original commit.

![Make a real working edit](images/22b-working-edit.png)

Entry: `In the regular VS Code pane, replace nightly with candidate. Leave it unsaved.`



## Return to the original evidence

Before: you made an unsaved candidate edit in the working counterpart. The original pinned review is back. The working edit survives separately; no review refresh is implied.

![Return to the original evidence](images/23-return-to-evidence.png)

Entry: `Click Return to Evidence Review.`



## A separate question: file history

The edit-and-return sequence is complete. This starts a different inspection. A dedicated history view opens. Select commits here to investigate how the file evolved.

![A separate question: file history](images/24-vscode-history.png)

Entry: `Optional detour: run Bygone: View Active File History for release.js.`



## Read the argument before the code

An authored tour arranges a change into chapters and scenes. The reading view tells the story; each step can open exact evidence.

![Read the argument before the code](images/25-tour-reader.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo present --tour release.bygone`



## Put a claim beside its evidence

A focused step highlights the relevant source in a pinned comparison. The narrative explains why the change matters, rather than reciting the diff.

![Put a claim beside its evidence](images/26-focused-step.png)

Entry: `Select a step • Show in code`



## Leave the path without losing it

Explore Files or Commits to test the explanation, then return to tour focus. Exploration does not change the authored comparison.

![Leave the path without losing it](images/27-explore-return.png)

Entry: `Files • Commits • Return to tour focus`



## Teach in conceptual stages

Deconstructed tours reorder changes into cumulative explanation stages. The screenshot uses Bygone’s public marker example; these stages are explicitly synthetic, not historical commits.

![Teach in conceptual stages](images/28-deconstructed.png)

Entry: `bygone present --tour examples/deconstructed-diff.bygone`



## Inspect validated symbol correspondence

Strand pairs the edited planRelease declaration across pinned revisions. The tree shows unmatched symbols and analysis limits. Inferred correspondence does not establish behavioral equivalence.

![Inspect validated symbol correspondence](images/31-symbol-tree.png)

Entry: `npm run correspondence:analyze -- feature --base main --engine bygone-strand --output correspondence.json`



## Turn review links into a tour

The real evidence exporter supplies claims and pinned links. The generated tour preserves producer assessments as claims, and explicitly marks verification as not recorded.

![Turn review links into a tour](images/29-evidence-tour.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo evidence tour imported.json --output evidence.bygone`



## Author an explanation from Git evidence

The authoring surface prepares a prompt grounded in the selected range. Write a .bygone source, validate anchors, and compile before sharing.

![Author an explanation from Git evidence](images/12-authoring.png)

Entry: `bygone tour context feature --base main --output context.json`



## Share a self-contained snapshot

An embedded minimal export opens without a repository or internet runtime. It includes whole referenced file contents, including surrounding and deleted text; review those bytes before sharing.

![Share a self-contained snapshot](images/30-portable.png)

Entry: `bygone tour export release.bygone --output tour.html --profile minimal --runtime embedded`



## Use dependency evidence to widen inspection

A real repair report identifies unchanged direct consumers of the modified module. An unchanged graph is not evidence of unchanged behavior.

![Use dependency evidence to widen inspection](images/32-dependencies.png)

Entry: `bygone evidence inspect review.json --dependencies dependencies.json`

Documentation card derived from actual dependency report; no graph UI is implied.

## Choose a host and entry point

Menus, drag/drop, CLI, deep links, and VS Code commands lead into the same core comparisons. Desktop handoff requires a configured local installation.

![Choose a host and entry point](images/33-hosts.png)

Entry: `bygone --help • bygone completion zsh`

Alternate entry routes are documented, not individually clicked in this capture run.

## Know what the view can prove

Interpret provenance, mutability and fallback labels before editing or drawing conclusions. Snapshot validity, test execution and human approval are separate facts.

![Know what the view can prove](images/34-limits.png)

Untracked and unsupported paths are documented coverage, not additional screenshots/tests in this run.

diff.title: narrative.md
diff.rightContent:
# Bygone: every view in context

Screenshot walkthrough for Bygone 0.11.1. Synthetic code and review data.

## Two files, one visual language

Blue ribbons connect changed regions; green marks additions. Local files can be edited. Use this for concrete before/after questions.

![Two files, one visual language](images/01-two-files.png)

Entry: `bygone before.js after.js`



## More than two versions

Add versions to see an evolution in one view. Fit changes how many panes are visible; the selected adjacent pair determines the active comparison.

![More than two versions](images/02-many-panels.png)

Entry: `bygone --diff v1.js v2.js v3.js v4.js v5.js`



## Start with directory differences

Compare trees, then drill into a changed path. This is a comparison inventory, not a merge tool.

![Start with directory differences](images/03-directories.png)

Entry: `bygone before/ after/`



## Search across the comparison

Find the same idea across panes, then inspect each result in its source context. Replacement is limited to writable sources.

![Search across the comparison](images/04-search.png)

Entry: `Cmd/Ctrl+F • Search Comparison • Search in Files`



## Start without a file

Use an untitled editable comparison for snippets. It has no Git provenance until you save or explicitly compare real sources.

![Start without a file](images/08-blank-editor.png)

Entry: `bygone --diff`



## Browse a repository through time

Files and commits provide two routes into history. Committed snapshots remain read-only.

![Browse a repository through time](images/05-repository-history.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo --history .`



## Follow one file through commits

Use a path when the question is how one file evolved. The history navigator selects concrete revisions.

![Follow one file through commits](images/06-file-history.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo release.js`



## Orient before reading every file

Branch review starts from the committed change against its merge base. The overview offers a reading order; dirty work is separate.

![Orient before reading every file](images/07-branch-review.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo review feature --base main`



## Name the endpoints explicitly

Compare commits and work states. HEAD and INDEX are read-only; WORKTREE can be writable. These labels are different kinds of evidence.

![Name the endpoints explicitly](images/09-git-snapshots.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo --git-diff HEAD~2 HEAD WORKTREE`



## One file, three saved states

HEAD: stable · Index: preview · Saved file: canary The same file appears under Staged Changes and Changes. These are two different comparisons.

![One file, three saved states](images/09a-scm-setup.png)

Entry: `Open Source Control with release.js selected.`



## Inspect what would be committed

Before: Source Control shows staged and unstaged work. Bygone compares HEAD stable → Index preview. Both sides are read-only; canary is excluded.

![Inspect what would be committed](images/11-scm-staged.png)

Entry: `Staged Changes → release.js → Open Staged Changes in Bygone.`



## Inspect what remains unstaged

Before: the staged comparison was stable → preview. The baseline is now Index preview; the writable side is the saved document canary.

![Inspect what remains unstaged](images/13-scm-working.png)

Entry: `Changes → release.js → Open Working Changes in Bygone.`



## Choose active-editor following

Before: release.js is saved as canary; index remains preview. The command is selected here. Press Enter to follow the active local document.

![Choose active-editor following](images/10a-follow-command.png)

Entry: `Focus release.js. Open the Command Palette and choose Bygone: Follow Active Editor.`



## See unsaved text in Bygone

Before: working document canary. Both views now show nightly. The dirty dot and Unsaved buffer label distinguish it from the saved file.

![See unsaved text in Bygone](images/10-follow-dirty.png)

Entry: `In the regular editor, replace canary with nightly. Leave the file unsaved.`



## Pin, then actually navigate away

Before: Bygone was following release.js. The native pane shows policy.js; pinned Bygone still shows release.js. Navigation did not replace it.

![Pin, then actually navigate away](images/14-pinned.png)

Entry: `Click Pin in Bygone. Open policy.js in the regular VS Code pane.`



## Return to the intended comparison

Before: release.js was pinned while policy.js was active. The active comparison is Index preview → unsaved nightly. Keep these endpoints while focusing a symbol.

![Return to the intended comparison](images/14b-resume-working.png)

Entry: `Source Control → Changes → release.js → Open Working Changes in Bygone.`



## Choose a symbol from the cursor

Before: the comparison contains the whole file. The selected command uses VS Code’s current cursor or selection. Press Enter to focus this declaration.

![Choose a symbol from the cursor](images/15a-symbol-command.png)

Entry: `Place the cursor inside planRelease. Choose Bygone: Compare Symbol in Bygone.`



## Narrow the view, preserve the comparison

Before: whole-file Index preview → working nightly. Both panes now contain planRelease. The same baseline and live document remain selected.

![Narrow the view, preserve the comparison](images/15-symbol-slice.png)

Entry: `Run Compare Symbol in Bygone from inside planRelease.`



## Edit in Bygone; see it in VS Code

Before: native editor and Bygone both showed nightly. Both now show dev. The index pane still shows preview; this is one shared, unsaved document.

![Edit in Bygone; see it in VS Code](images/16-synced-edit.png)

Entry: `In Bygone’s right-hand symbol pane, replace nightly with dev.`



## Undo once, update both views

Before: the previous edit changed nightly → dev. The regular editor and Bygone both return to nightly. The file is still unsaved.

![Undo once, update both views](images/17-shared-undo.png)

Entry: `Click Undo in Bygone.`



## Save the document, keep the index

Before: working document nightly was dirty; index was preview. Saved buffer replaces Unsaved buffer, and the dirty dot clears. The index remains preview.

![Save the document, keep the index](images/18-save-no-stage.png)

Entry: `Click Save in Bygone.`



## Open a saved review

Before: you were editing a live working document. The review displays its pinned Git identities and cited source references. It is a separate artifact.

![Open a saved review](images/19-evidence-review.png)

Entry: `Run Bygone: Open Evidence Review and select review.json for this repository.`



## Read the exact cited file diff

Before: the review listed a source citation. Bygone opens the review’s committed comparison. Your working nightly text is not substituted into it.

![Read the exact cited file diff](images/21-pinned-diff.png)

Entry: `In Evidence Review, choose Pinned file diff for planRelease.`



## Open a live counterpart for editing

Before: you were inspecting an immutable committed diff. A separate working view opens with Return to Evidence Review available. The live value is nightly.

![Open a live counterpart for editing](images/22-evidence-repair.png)

Entry: `Return to Evidence Review. Choose Edit working counterpart for the same reference.`



## Make a real working edit

Before: the live counterpart showed nightly. The regular document now contains candidate. The captured review still refers to its original commit.

![Make a real working edit](images/22b-working-edit.png)

Entry: `In the regular VS Code pane, replace nightly with candidate. Leave it unsaved.`



## Return to the original evidence

Before: you made an unsaved candidate edit in the working counterpart. The original pinned review is back. The working edit survives separately; no review refresh is implied.

![Return to the original evidence](images/23-return-to-evidence.png)

Entry: `Click Return to Evidence Review.`



## A separate question: file history

The edit-and-return sequence is complete. This starts a different inspection. A dedicated history view opens. Select commits here to investigate how the file evolved.

![A separate question: file history](images/24-vscode-history.png)

Entry: `Optional detour: run Bygone: View Active File History for release.js.`



## Read the argument before the code

An authored tour arranges a change into chapters and scenes. The reading view tells the story; each step can open exact evidence.

![Read the argument before the code](images/25-tour-reader.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo present --tour release.bygone`



## Put a claim beside its evidence

A focused step highlights the relevant source in a pinned comparison. The narrative explains why the change matters, rather than reciting the diff.

![Put a claim beside its evidence](images/26-focused-step.png)

Entry: `Select a step • Show in code`



## Leave the path without losing it

Explore Files or Commits to test the explanation, then return to tour focus. Exploration does not change the authored comparison.

![Leave the path without losing it](images/27-explore-return.png)

Entry: `Files • Commits • Return to tour focus`



## Teach in conceptual stages

Deconstructed tours reorder changes into cumulative explanation stages. The screenshot uses Bygone’s public marker example; these stages are explicitly synthetic, not historical commits.

![Teach in conceptual stages](images/28-deconstructed.png)

Entry: `bygone present --tour examples/deconstructed-diff.bygone`



## Inspect validated symbol correspondence

Strand pairs the edited planRelease declaration across pinned revisions. The tree shows unmatched symbols and analysis limits. Inferred correspondence does not establish behavioral equivalence.

![Inspect validated symbol correspondence](images/31-symbol-tree.png)

Entry: `npm run correspondence:analyze -- feature --base main --engine bygone-strand --output correspondence.json`



## Turn review links into a tour

The real evidence exporter supplies claims and pinned links. The generated tour preserves producer assessments as claims, and explicitly marks verification as not recorded.

![Turn review links into a tour](images/29-evidence-tour.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo evidence tour imported.json --output evidence.bygone`



## Author an explanation from Git evidence

The authoring surface prepares a prompt grounded in the selected range. Write a .bygone source, validate anchors, and compile before sharing.

![Author an explanation from Git evidence](images/12-authoring.png)

Entry: `bygone tour context feature --base main --output context.json`



## Share a self-contained snapshot

An embedded minimal export opens without a repository or internet runtime. It includes whole referenced file contents, including surrounding and deleted text; review those bytes before sharing.

![Share a self-contained snapshot](images/30-portable.png)

Entry: `bygone tour export release.bygone --output tour.html --profile minimal --runtime embedded`



## Use dependency evidence to widen inspection

A real repair report identifies unchanged direct consumers of the modified module. An unchanged graph is not evidence of unchanged behavior.

![Use dependency evidence to widen inspection](images/32-dependencies.png)

Entry: `bygone evidence inspect review.json --dependencies dependencies.json`

Documentation card derived from actual dependency report; no graph UI is implied.

## Choose a host and entry point

Menus, drag/drop, CLI, deep links, and VS Code commands lead into the same core comparisons. Desktop handoff requires a configured local installation.

![Choose a host and entry point](images/33-hosts.png)

Entry: `bygone --help • bygone completion zsh`

Alternate entry routes are documented, not individually clicked in this capture run.

## Know what the view can prove

Interpret provenance, mutability and fallback labels before editing or drawing conclusions. Snapshot validity, test execution and human approval are separate facts.

![Know what the view can prove](images/34-limits.png)

Untracked and unsupported paths are documented coverage, not additional screenshots/tests in this run.

# Bygone: every view in context

Screenshot walkthrough for Bygone 0.11.1. Synthetic code and review data.

## Two files, one visual language

Blue ribbons connect changed regions; green marks additions. Local files can be edited. Use this for concrete before/after questions.

![Two files, one visual language](images/01-two-files.png)

Entry: `bygone before.js after.js`



## More than two versions

Add versions to see an evolution in one view. Fit changes how many panes are visible; the selected adjacent pair determines the active comparison.

![More than two versions](images/02-many-panels.png)

Entry: `bygone --diff v1.js v2.js v3.js v4.js v5.js`



## Start with directory differences

Compare trees, then drill into a changed path. This is a comparison inventory, not a merge tool.

![Start with directory differences](images/03-directories.png)

Entry: `bygone before/ after/`



## Search across the comparison

Find the same idea across panes, then inspect each result in its source context. Replacement is limited to writable sources.

![Search across the comparison](images/04-search.png)

Entry: `Cmd/Ctrl+F • Search Comparison • Search in Files`



## Start without a file

Use an untitled editable comparison for snippets. It has no Git provenance until you save or explicitly compare real sources.

![Start without a file](images/08-blank-editor.png)

Entry: `bygone --diff`



## Browse a repository through time

Files and commits provide two routes into history. Committed snapshots remain read-only.

![Browse a repository through time](images/05-repository-history.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo --history .`



## Follow one file through commits

Use a path when the question is how one file evolved. The history navigator selects concrete revisions.

![Follow one file through commits](images/06-file-history.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo release.js`



## Orient before reading every file

Branch review starts from the committed change against its merge base. The overview offers a reading order; dirty work is separate.

![Orient before reading every file](images/07-branch-review.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo review feature --base main`



## Name the endpoints explicitly

Compare commits and work states. HEAD and INDEX are read-only; WORKTREE can be writable. These labels are different kinds of evidence.

![Name the endpoints explicitly](images/09-git-snapshots.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo --git-diff HEAD~2 HEAD WORKTREE`



## One file, three saved states

HEAD: stable · Index: preview · Saved file: canary The same file appears under Staged Changes and Changes. These are two different comparisons.

![One file, three saved states](images/09a-scm-setup.png)

Entry: `Open Source Control with release.js selected.`



## Inspect what would be committed

Before: Source Control shows staged and unstaged work. Bygone compares HEAD stable → Index preview. Both sides are read-only; canary is excluded.

![Inspect what would be committed](images/11-scm-staged.png)

Entry: `Staged Changes → release.js → Open Staged Changes in Bygone.`



## Inspect what remains unstaged

Before: the staged comparison was stable → preview. The baseline is now Index preview; the writable side is the saved document canary.

![Inspect what remains unstaged](images/13-scm-working.png)

Entry: `Changes → release.js → Open Working Changes in Bygone.`



## Choose active-editor following

Before: release.js is saved as canary; index remains preview. The command is selected here. Press Enter to follow the active local document.

![Choose active-editor following](images/10a-follow-command.png)

Entry: `Focus release.js. Open the Command Palette and choose Bygone: Follow Active Editor.`



## See unsaved text in Bygone

Before: working document canary. Both views now show nightly. The dirty dot and Unsaved buffer label distinguish it from the saved file.

![See unsaved text in Bygone](images/10-follow-dirty.png)

Entry: `In the regular editor, replace canary with nightly. Leave the file unsaved.`



## Pin, then actually navigate away

Before: Bygone was following release.js. The native pane shows policy.js; pinned Bygone still shows release.js. Navigation did not replace it.

![Pin, then actually navigate away](images/14-pinned.png)

Entry: `Click Pin in Bygone. Open policy.js in the regular VS Code pane.`



## Return to the intended comparison

Before: release.js was pinned while policy.js was active. The active comparison is Index preview → unsaved nightly. Keep these endpoints while focusing a symbol.

![Return to the intended comparison](images/14b-resume-working.png)

Entry: `Source Control → Changes → release.js → Open Working Changes in Bygone.`



## Choose a symbol from the cursor

Before: the comparison contains the whole file. The selected command uses VS Code’s current cursor or selection. Press Enter to focus this declaration.

![Choose a symbol from the cursor](images/15a-symbol-command.png)

Entry: `Place the cursor inside planRelease. Choose Bygone: Compare Symbol in Bygone.`



## Narrow the view, preserve the comparison

Before: whole-file Index preview → working nightly. Both panes now contain planRelease. The same baseline and live document remain selected.

![Narrow the view, preserve the comparison](images/15-symbol-slice.png)

Entry: `Run Compare Symbol in Bygone from inside planRelease.`



## Edit in Bygone; see it in VS Code

Before: native editor and Bygone both showed nightly. Both now show dev. The index pane still shows preview; this is one shared, unsaved document.

![Edit in Bygone; see it in VS Code](images/16-synced-edit.png)

Entry: `In Bygone’s right-hand symbol pane, replace nightly with dev.`



## Undo once, update both views

Before: the previous edit changed nightly → dev. The regular editor and Bygone both return to nightly. The file is still unsaved.

![Undo once, update both views](images/17-shared-undo.png)

Entry: `Click Undo in Bygone.`



## Save the document, keep the index

Before: working document nightly was dirty; index was preview. Saved buffer replaces Unsaved buffer, and the dirty dot clears. The index remains preview.

![Save the document, keep the index](images/18-save-no-stage.png)

Entry: `Click Save in Bygone.`



## Open a saved review

Before: you were editing a live working document. The review displays its pinned Git identities and cited source references. It is a separate artifact.

![Open a saved review](images/19-evidence-review.png)

Entry: `Run Bygone: Open Evidence Review and select review.json for this repository.`



## Read the exact cited file diff

Before: the review listed a source citation. Bygone opens the review’s committed comparison. Your working nightly text is not substituted into it.

![Read the exact cited file diff](images/21-pinned-diff.png)

Entry: `In Evidence Review, choose Pinned file diff for planRelease.`



## Open a live counterpart for editing

Before: you were inspecting an immutable committed diff. A separate working view opens with Return to Evidence Review available. The live value is nightly.

![Open a live counterpart for editing](images/22-evidence-repair.png)

Entry: `Return to Evidence Review. Choose Edit working counterpart for the same reference.`



## Make a real working edit

Before: the live counterpart showed nightly. The regular document now contains candidate. The captured review still refers to its original commit.

![Make a real working edit](images/22b-working-edit.png)

Entry: `In the regular VS Code pane, replace nightly with candidate. Leave it unsaved.`



## Return to the original evidence

Before: you made an unsaved candidate edit in the working counterpart. The original pinned review is back. The working edit survives separately; no review refresh is implied.

![Return to the original evidence](images/23-return-to-evidence.png)

Entry: `Click Return to Evidence Review.`



## A separate question: file history

The edit-and-return sequence is complete. This starts a different inspection. A dedicated history view opens. Select commits here to investigate how the file evolved.

![A separate question: file history](images/24-vscode-history.png)

Entry: `Optional detour: run Bygone: View Active File History for release.js.`



## Read the argument before the code

An authored tour arranges a change into chapters and scenes. The reading view tells the story; each step can open exact evidence.

![Read the argument before the code](images/25-tour-reader.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo present --tour release.bygone`



## Put a claim beside its evidence

A focused step highlights the relevant source in a pinned comparison. The narrative explains why the change matters, rather than reciting the diff.

![Put a claim beside its evidence](images/26-focused-step.png)

Entry: `Select a step • Show in code`



## Leave the path without losing it

Explore Files or Commits to test the explanation, then return to tour focus. Exploration does not change the authored comparison.

![Leave the path without losing it](images/27-explore-return.png)

Entry: `Files • Commits • Return to tour focus`



## Teach in conceptual stages

Deconstructed tours reorder changes into cumulative explanation stages. The screenshot uses Bygone’s public marker example; these stages are explicitly synthetic, not historical commits.

![Teach in conceptual stages](images/28-deconstructed.png)

Entry: `bygone present --tour examples/deconstructed-diff.bygone`



## Inspect validated symbol correspondence

Strand pairs the edited planRelease declaration across pinned revisions. The tree shows unmatched symbols and analysis limits. Inferred correspondence does not establish behavioral equivalence.

![Inspect validated symbol correspondence](images/31-symbol-tree.png)

Entry: `npm run correspondence:analyze -- feature --base main --engine bygone-strand --output correspondence.json`



## Turn review links into a tour

The real evidence exporter supplies claims and pinned links. The generated tour preserves producer assessments as claims, and explicitly marks verification as not recorded.

![Turn review links into a tour](images/29-evidence-tour.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo evidence tour imported.json --output evidence.bygone`



## Author an explanation from Git evidence

The authoring surface prepares a prompt grounded in the selected range. Write a .bygone source, validate anchors, and compile before sharing.

![Author an explanation from Git evidence](images/12-authoring.png)

Entry: `bygone tour context feature --base main --output context.json`



## Share a self-contained snapshot

An embedded minimal export opens without a repository or internet runtime. It includes whole referenced file contents, including surrounding and deleted text; review those bytes before sharing.

![Share a self-contained snapshot](images/30-portable.png)

Entry: `bygone tour export release.bygone --output tour.html --profile minimal --runtime embedded`



## Use dependency evidence to widen inspection

A real repair report identifies unchanged direct consumers of the modified module. An unchanged graph is not evidence of unchanged behavior.

![Use dependency evidence to widen inspection](images/32-dependencies.png)

Entry: `bygone evidence inspect review.json --dependencies dependencies.json`

Documentation card derived from actual dependency report; no graph UI is implied.

## Choose a host and entry point

Menus, drag/drop, CLI, deep links, and VS Code commands lead into the same core comparisons. Desktop handoff requires a configured local installation.

![Choose a host and entry point](images/33-hosts.png)

Entry: `bygone --help • bygone completion zsh`

Alternate entry routes are documented, not individually clicked in this capture run.

## Know what the view can prove

Interpret provenance, mutability and fallback labels before editing or drawing conclusions. Snapshot validity, test execution and human approval are separate facts.

![Know what the view can prove](images/34-limits.png)

Untracked and unsupported paths are documented coverage, not additional screenshots/tests in this run.

# Bygone: every view in context

Screenshot walkthrough for Bygone 0.11.1. Synthetic code and review data.

## Two files, one visual language

Blue ribbons connect changed regions; green marks additions. Local files can be edited. Use this for concrete before/after questions.

![Two files, one visual language](images/01-two-files.png)

Entry: `bygone before.js after.js`



## More than two versions

Add versions to see an evolution in one view. Fit changes how many panes are visible; the selected adjacent pair determines the active comparison.

![More than two versions](images/02-many-panels.png)

Entry: `bygone --diff v1.js v2.js v3.js v4.js v5.js`



## Start with directory differences

Compare trees, then drill into a changed path. This is a comparison inventory, not a merge tool.

![Start with directory differences](images/03-directories.png)

Entry: `bygone before/ after/`



## Search across the comparison

Find the same idea across panes, then inspect each result in its source context. Replacement is limited to writable sources.

![Search across the comparison](images/04-search.png)

Entry: `Cmd/Ctrl+F • Search Comparison • Search in Files`



## Start without a file

Use an untitled editable comparison for snippets. It has no Git provenance until you save or explicitly compare real sources.

![Start without a file](images/08-blank-editor.png)

Entry: `bygone --diff`



## Browse a repository through time

Files and commits provide two routes into history. Committed snapshots remain read-only.

![Browse a repository through time](images/05-repository-history.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo --history .`



## Follow one file through commits

Use a path when the question is how one file evolved. The history navigator selects concrete revisions.

![Follow one file through commits](images/06-file-history.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo release.js`



## Orient before reading every file

Branch review starts from the committed change against its merge base. The overview offers a reading order; dirty work is separate.

![Orient before reading every file](images/07-branch-review.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo review feature --base main`



## Name the endpoints explicitly

Compare commits and work states. HEAD and INDEX are read-only; WORKTREE can be writable. These labels are different kinds of evidence.

![Name the endpoints explicitly](images/09-git-snapshots.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo --git-diff HEAD~2 HEAD WORKTREE`



## One file, three saved states

HEAD: stable · Index: preview · Saved file: canary The same file appears under Staged Changes and Changes. These are two different comparisons.

![One file, three saved states](images/09a-scm-setup.png)

Entry: `Open Source Control with release.js selected.`



## Inspect what would be committed

Before: Source Control shows staged and unstaged work. Bygone compares HEAD stable → Index preview. Both sides are read-only; canary is excluded.

![Inspect what would be committed](images/11-scm-staged.png)

Entry: `Staged Changes → release.js → Open Staged Changes in Bygone.`



## Inspect what remains unstaged

Before: the staged comparison was stable → preview. The baseline is now Index preview; the writable side is the saved document canary.

![Inspect what remains unstaged](images/13-scm-working.png)

Entry: `Changes → release.js → Open Working Changes in Bygone.`



## Choose active-editor following

Before: release.js is saved as canary; index remains preview. The command is selected here. Press Enter to follow the active local document.

![Choose active-editor following](images/10a-follow-command.png)

Entry: `Focus release.js. Open the Command Palette and choose Bygone: Follow Active Editor.`



## See unsaved text in Bygone

Before: working document canary. Both views now show nightly. The dirty dot and Unsaved buffer label distinguish it from the saved file.

![See unsaved text in Bygone](images/10-follow-dirty.png)

Entry: `In the regular editor, replace canary with nightly. Leave the file unsaved.`



## Pin, then actually navigate away

Before: Bygone was following release.js. The native pane shows policy.js; pinned Bygone still shows release.js. Navigation did not replace it.

![Pin, then actually navigate away](images/14-pinned.png)

Entry: `Click Pin in Bygone. Open policy.js in the regular VS Code pane.`



## Return to the intended comparison

Before: release.js was pinned while policy.js was active. The active comparison is Index preview → unsaved nightly. Keep these endpoints while focusing a symbol.

![Return to the intended comparison](images/14b-resume-working.png)

Entry: `Source Control → Changes → release.js → Open Working Changes in Bygone.`



## Choose a symbol from the cursor

Before: the comparison contains the whole file. The selected command uses VS Code’s current cursor or selection. Press Enter to focus this declaration.

![Choose a symbol from the cursor](images/15a-symbol-command.png)

Entry: `Place the cursor inside planRelease. Choose Bygone: Compare Symbol in Bygone.`



## Narrow the view, preserve the comparison

Before: whole-file Index preview → working nightly. Both panes now contain planRelease. The same baseline and live document remain selected.

![Narrow the view, preserve the comparison](images/15-symbol-slice.png)

Entry: `Run Compare Symbol in Bygone from inside planRelease.`



## Edit in Bygone; see it in VS Code

Before: native editor and Bygone both showed nightly. Both now show dev. The index pane still shows preview; this is one shared, unsaved document.

![Edit in Bygone; see it in VS Code](images/16-synced-edit.png)

Entry: `In Bygone’s right-hand symbol pane, replace nightly with dev.`



## Undo once, update both views

Before: the previous edit changed nightly → dev. The regular editor and Bygone both return to nightly. The file is still unsaved.

![Undo once, update both views](images/17-shared-undo.png)

Entry: `Click Undo in Bygone.`



## Save the document, keep the index

Before: working document nightly was dirty; index was preview. Saved buffer replaces Unsaved buffer, and the dirty dot clears. The index remains preview.

![Save the document, keep the index](images/18-save-no-stage.png)

Entry: `Click Save in Bygone.`



## Open a saved review

Before: you were editing a live working document. The review displays its pinned Git identities and cited source references. It is a separate artifact.

![Open a saved review](images/19-evidence-review.png)

Entry: `Run Bygone: Open Evidence Review and select review.json for this repository.`



## Read the exact cited file diff

Before: the review listed a source citation. Bygone opens the review’s committed comparison. Your working nightly text is not substituted into it.

![Read the exact cited file diff](images/21-pinned-diff.png)

Entry: `In Evidence Review, choose Pinned file diff for planRelease.`



## Open a live counterpart for editing

Before: you were inspecting an immutable committed diff. A separate working view opens with Return to Evidence Review available. The live value is nightly.

![Open a live counterpart for editing](images/22-evidence-repair.png)

Entry: `Return to Evidence Review. Choose Edit working counterpart for the same reference.`



## Make a real working edit

Before: the live counterpart showed nightly. The regular document now contains candidate. The captured review still refers to its original commit.

![Make a real working edit](images/22b-working-edit.png)

Entry: `In the regular VS Code pane, replace nightly with candidate. Leave it unsaved.`



## Return to the original evidence

Before: you made an unsaved candidate edit in the working counterpart. The original pinned review is back. The working edit survives separately; no review refresh is implied.

![Return to the original evidence](images/23-return-to-evidence.png)

Entry: `Click Return to Evidence Review.`



## A separate question: file history

The edit-and-return sequence is complete. This starts a different inspection. A dedicated history view opens. Select commits here to investigate how the file evolved.

![A separate question: file history](images/24-vscode-history.png)

Entry: `Optional detour: run Bygone: View Active File History for release.js.`



## Read the argument before the code

An authored tour arranges a change into chapters and scenes. The reading view tells the story; each step can open exact evidence.

![Read the argument before the code](images/25-tour-reader.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo present --tour release.bygone`



## Put a claim beside its evidence

A focused step highlights the relevant source in a pinned comparison. The narrative explains why the change matters, rather than reciting the diff.

![Put a claim beside its evidence](images/26-focused-step.png)

Entry: `Select a step • Show in code`



## Leave the path without losing it

Explore Files or Commits to test the explanation, then return to tour focus. Exploration does not change the authored comparison.

![Leave the path without losing it](images/27-explore-return.png)

Entry: `Files • Commits • Return to tour focus`



## Teach in conceptual stages

Deconstructed tours reorder changes into cumulative explanation stages. The screenshot uses Bygone’s public marker example; these stages are explicitly synthetic, not historical commits.

![Teach in conceptual stages](images/28-deconstructed.png)

Entry: `bygone present --tour examples/deconstructed-diff.bygone`



## Inspect validated symbol correspondence

Strand pairs the edited planRelease declaration across pinned revisions. The tree shows unmatched symbols and analysis limits. Inferred correspondence does not establish behavioral equivalence.

![Inspect validated symbol correspondence](images/31-symbol-tree.png)

Entry: `npm run correspondence:analyze -- feature --base main --engine bygone-strand --output correspondence.json`



## Turn review links into a tour

The real evidence exporter supplies claims and pinned links. The generated tour preserves producer assessments as claims, and explicitly marks verification as not recorded.

![Turn review links into a tour](images/29-evidence-tour.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo evidence tour imported.json --output evidence.bygone`



## Author an explanation from Git evidence

The authoring surface prepares a prompt grounded in the selected range. Write a .bygone source, validate anchors, and compile before sharing.

![Author an explanation from Git evidence](images/12-authoring.png)

Entry: `bygone tour context feature --base main --output context.json`



## Share a self-contained snapshot

An embedded minimal export opens without a repository or internet runtime. It includes whole referenced file contents, including surrounding and deleted text; review those bytes before sharing.

![Share a self-contained snapshot](images/30-portable.png)

Entry: `bygone tour export release.bygone --output tour.html --profile minimal --runtime embedded`



## Use dependency evidence to widen inspection

A real repair report identifies unchanged direct consumers of the modified module. An unchanged graph is not evidence of unchanged behavior.

![Use dependency evidence to widen inspection](images/32-dependencies.png)

Entry: `bygone evidence inspect review.json --dependencies dependencies.json`

Documentation card derived from actual dependency report; no graph UI is implied.

## Choose a host and entry point

Menus, drag/drop, CLI, deep links, and VS Code commands lead into the same core comparisons. Desktop handoff requires a configured local installation.

![Choose a host and entry point](images/33-hosts.png)

Entry: `bygone --help • bygone completion zsh`

Alternate entry routes are documented, not individually clicked in this capture run.

## Know what the view can prove

Interpret provenance, mutability and fallback labels before editing or drawing conclusions. Snapshot validity, test execution and human approval are separate facts.

![Know what the view can prove](images/34-limits.png)

Untracked and unsupported paths are documented coverage, not additional screenshots/tests in this run.

## Inspect what remains unstaged

scenes.summary: Open a saved review, inspect its exact committed diff, make a real edit in a separate live counterpart, then return to the unchanged review. An optional file-history detour closes the sequence.
scenes.takeaway: Editing a file must not silently alter the evidence being reviewed.

Find the same idea across panes, then inspect each result in its source context. Replacement is limited to writable sources.

Use an untitled editable comparison for snippets. It has no Git provenance until you save or explicitly compare real sources.

## Follow one file through commits

Use a path when the question is how one file evolved. The history navigator selects concrete revisions.

![Follow one file through commits](images/06-file-history.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo release.js`



## Orient before reading every file

Branch review starts from the committed change against its merge base. The overview offers a reading order; dirty work is separate.

![Orient before reading every file](images/07-branch-review.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo review feature --base main`



## Name the endpoints explicitly

Compare commits and work states. HEAD and INDEX are read-only; WORKTREE can be writable. These labels are different kinds of evidence.

![Name the endpoints explicitly](images/09-git-snapshots.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo --git-diff HEAD~2 HEAD WORKTREE`



## One file, three saved states

HEAD: stable · Index: preview · Saved file: canary The same file appears under Staged Changes and Changes. These are two different comparisons.

![One file, three saved states](images/09a-scm-setup.png)

Entry: `Open Source Control with release.js selected.`



## Inspect what would be committed

Before: Source Control shows staged and unstaged work. Bygone compares HEAD stable → Index preview. Both sides are read-only; canary is excluded.

![Inspect what would be committed](images/11-scm-staged.png)

Entry: `Staged Changes → release.js → Open Staged Changes in Bygone.`



## Inspect what remains unstaged

Before: the staged comparison was stable → preview. The baseline is now Index preview; the writable side is the saved document canary.

![Inspect what remains unstaged](images/13-scm-working.png)

Entry: `Changes → release.js → Open Working Changes in Bygone.`



## Choose active-editor following

Before: release.js is saved as canary; index remains preview. The command is selected here. Press Enter to follow the active local document.

![Choose active-editor following](images/10a-follow-command.png)

Entry: `Focus release.js. Open the Command Palette and choose Bygone: Follow Active Editor.`



## See unsaved text in Bygone

Before: working document canary. Both views now show nightly. The dirty dot and Unsaved buffer label distinguish it from the saved file.

![See unsaved text in Bygone](images/10-follow-dirty.png)

Entry: `In the regular editor, replace canary with nightly. Leave the file unsaved.`



## Pin, then actually navigate away

Before: Bygone was following release.js. The native pane shows policy.js; pinned Bygone still shows release.js. Navigation did not replace it.

![Pin, then actually navigate away](images/14-pinned.png)

Entry: `Click Pin in Bygone. Open policy.js in the regular VS Code pane.`



## Return to the intended comparison

Before: release.js was pinned while policy.js was active. The active comparison is Index preview → unsaved nightly. Keep these endpoints while focusing a symbol.

![Return to the intended comparison](images/14b-resume-working.png)

Entry: `Source Control → Changes → release.js → Open Working Changes in Bygone.`



## Choose a symbol from the cursor

Before: the comparison contains the whole file. The selected command uses VS Code’s current cursor or selection. Press Enter to focus this declaration.

![Choose a symbol from the cursor](images/15a-symbol-command.png)

Entry: `Place the cursor inside planRelease. Choose Bygone: Compare Symbol in Bygone.`



## Narrow the view, preserve the comparison

Before: whole-file Index preview → working nightly. Both panes now contain planRelease. The same baseline and live document remain selected.

![Narrow the view, preserve the comparison](images/15-symbol-slice.png)

Entry: `Run Compare Symbol in Bygone from inside planRelease.`



## Edit in Bygone; see it in VS Code

Before: native editor and Bygone both showed nightly. Both now show dev. The index pane still shows preview; this is one shared, unsaved document.

![Edit in Bygone; see it in VS Code](images/16-synced-edit.png)

Entry: `In Bygone’s right-hand symbol pane, replace nightly with dev.`



## Undo once, update both views

Before: the previous edit changed nightly → dev. The regular editor and Bygone both return to nightly. The file is still unsaved.

![Undo once, update both views](images/17-shared-undo.png)

Entry: `Click Undo in Bygone.`



## Save the document, keep the index

Before: working document nightly was dirty; index was preview. Saved buffer replaces Unsaved buffer, and the dirty dot clears. The index remains preview.

![Save the document, keep the index](images/18-save-no-stage.png)

Entry: `Click Save in Bygone.`



## Open a saved review

Before: you were editing a live working document. The review displays its pinned Git identities and cited source references. It is a separate artifact.

![Open a saved review](images/19-evidence-review.png)

Entry: `Run Bygone: Open Evidence Review and select review.json for this repository.`



## Read the exact cited file diff

Before: the review listed a source citation. Bygone opens the review’s committed comparison. Your working nightly text is not substituted into it.

![Read the exact cited file diff](images/21-pinned-diff.png)

Entry: `In Evidence Review, choose Pinned file diff for planRelease.`



## Open a live counterpart for editing

Before: you were inspecting an immutable committed diff. A separate working view opens with Return to Evidence Review available. The live value is nightly.

![Open a live counterpart for editing](images/22-evidence-repair.png)

Entry: `Return to Evidence Review. Choose Edit working counterpart for the same reference.`



## Make a real working edit

Before: the live counterpart showed nightly. The regular document now contains candidate. The captured review still refers to its original commit.

![Make a real working edit](images/22b-working-edit.png)

Entry: `In the regular VS Code pane, replace nightly with candidate. Leave it unsaved.`



## Return to the original evidence

Before: you made an unsaved candidate edit in the working counterpart. The original pinned review is back. The working edit survives separately; no review refresh is implied.

![Return to the original evidence](images/23-return-to-evidence.png)

Entry: `Click Return to Evidence Review.`



## A separate question: file history

The edit-and-return sequence is complete. This starts a different inspection. A dedicated history view opens. Select commits here to investigate how the file evolved.

![A separate question: file history](images/24-vscode-history.png)

Entry: `Optional detour: run Bygone: View Active File History for release.js.`



## Read the argument before the code

An authored tour arranges a change into chapters and scenes. The reading view tells the story; each step can open exact evidence.

![Read the argument before the code](images/25-tour-reader.png)

## Put a claim beside its evidence

A focused step highlights the relevant source in a pinned comparison. The narrative explains why the change matters, rather than reciting the diff.

![Put a claim beside its evidence](images/26-focused-step.png)

Entry: `Select a step • Show in code`



## Leave the path without losing it

![Leave the path without losing it](images/27-explore-return.png)

Entry: `Files • Commits • Return to tour focus`



## Teach in conceptual stages

Deconstructed tours reorder changes into cumulative explanation stages. The screenshot uses Bygone’s public marker example; these stages are explicitly synthetic, not historical commits.

![Teach in conceptual stages](images/28-deconstructed.png)

Entry: `bygone present --tour examples/deconstructed-diff.bygone`



## Inspect validated symbol correspondence

Strand pairs the edited planRelease declaration across pinned revisions. The tree shows unmatched symbols and analysis limits. Inferred correspondence does not establish behavioral equivalence.

![Inspect validated symbol correspondence](images/31-symbol-tree.png)

Entry: `npm run correspondence:analyze -- feature --base main --engine bygone-strand --output correspondence.json`



## Turn review links into a tour

The real evidence exporter supplies claims and pinned links. The generated tour preserves producer assessments as claims, and explicitly marks verification as not recorded.

![Turn review links into a tour](images/29-evidence-tour.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo evidence tour imported.json --output evidence.bygone`



## Author an explanation from Git evidence

The authoring surface prepares a prompt grounded in the selected range. Write a .bygone source, validate anchors, and compile before sharing.

![Author an explanation from Git evidence](images/12-authoring.png)

Entry: `bygone tour context feature --base main --output context.json`



## Share a self-contained snapshot

An embedded minimal export opens without a repository or internet runtime. It includes whole referenced file contents, including surrounding and deleted text; review those bytes before sharing.

![Share a self-contained snapshot](images/30-portable.png)

Entry: `bygone tour export release.bygone --output tour.html --profile minimal --runtime embedded`



## Use dependency evidence to widen inspection

A real repair report identifies unchanged direct consumers of the modified module. An unchanged graph is not evidence of unchanged behavior.

![Use dependency evidence to widen inspection](images/32-dependencies.png)

Entry: `bygone evidence inspect review.json --dependencies dependencies.json`

Documentation card derived from actual dependency report; no graph UI is implied.

## Choose a host and entry point

Menus, drag/drop, CLI, deep links, and VS Code commands lead into the same core comparisons. Desktop handoff requires a configured local installation.

![Choose a host and entry point](images/33-hosts.png)

Entry: `bygone --help • bygone completion zsh`

Alternate entry routes are documented, not individually clicked in this capture run.

## Know what the view can prove

Interpret provenance, mutability and fallback labels before editing or drawing conclusions. Snapshot validity, test execution and human approval are separate facts.

![Know what the view can prove](images/34-limits.png)

Untracked and unsupported paths are documented coverage, not additional screenshots/tests in this run.

![Two files, one visual language](images/01-two-files.png)

Entry: `bygone before.js after.js`



## More than two versions

Add versions to see an evolution in one view. Fit changes how many panes are visible; the selected adjacent pair determines the active comparison.

![More than two versions](images/02-many-panels.png)

Entry: `bygone --diff v1.js v2.js v3.js v4.js v5.js`



## Start with directory differences

Compare trees, then drill into a changed path. This is a comparison inventory, not a merge tool.

![Start with directory differences](images/03-directories.png)

Entry: `bygone before/ after/`



## Search across the comparison

Find the same idea across panes, then inspect each result in its source context. Replacement is limited to writable sources.

![Search across the comparison](images/04-search.png)

Entry: `Cmd/Ctrl+F • Search Comparison • Search in Files`



## Start without a file

Use an untitled editable comparison for snippets. It has no Git provenance until you save or explicitly compare real sources.

![Start without a file](images/08-blank-editor.png)

Entry: `bygone --diff`



## Browse a repository through time

Files and commits provide two routes into history. Committed snapshots remain read-only.

![Browse a repository through time](images/05-repository-history.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo --history .`



## Follow one file through commits

Use a path when the question is how one file evolved. The history navigator selects concrete revisions.

![Follow one file through commits](images/06-file-history.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo release.js`



## Orient before reading every file

Branch review starts from the committed change against its merge base. The overview offers a reading order; dirty work is separate.

![Orient before reading every file](images/07-branch-review.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo review feature --base main`



## Name the endpoints explicitly

Compare commits and work states. HEAD and INDEX are read-only; WORKTREE can be writable. These labels are different kinds of evidence.

![Name the endpoints explicitly](images/09-git-snapshots.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo --git-diff HEAD~2 HEAD WORKTREE`



## One file, three saved states

HEAD: stable · Index: preview · Saved file: canary The same file appears under Staged Changes and Changes. These are two different comparisons.

![One file, three saved states](images/09a-scm-setup.png)

Entry: `Open Source Control with release.js selected.`



## Inspect what would be committed

Before: Source Control shows staged and unstaged work. Bygone compares HEAD stable → Index preview. Both sides are read-only; canary is excluded.

![Inspect what would be committed](images/11-scm-staged.png)

Entry: `Staged Changes → release.js → Open Staged Changes in Bygone.`



## Inspect what remains unstaged

Before: the staged comparison was stable → preview. The baseline is now Index preview; the writable side is the saved document canary.

![Inspect what remains unstaged](images/13-scm-working.png)

Entry: `Changes → release.js → Open Working Changes in Bygone.`



## Choose active-editor following

Before: release.js is saved as canary; index remains preview. The command is selected here. Press Enter to follow the active local document.

![Choose active-editor following](images/10a-follow-command.png)

Entry: `Focus release.js. Open the Command Palette and choose Bygone: Follow Active Editor.`



## See unsaved text in Bygone

Before: working document canary. Both views now show nightly. The dirty dot and Unsaved buffer label distinguish it from the saved file.

![See unsaved text in Bygone](images/10-follow-dirty.png)

Entry: `In the regular editor, replace canary with nightly. Leave the file unsaved.`



## Pin, then actually navigate away

Before: Bygone was following release.js. The native pane shows policy.js; pinned Bygone still shows release.js. Navigation did not replace it.

![Pin, then actually navigate away](images/14-pinned.png)

Entry: `Click Pin in Bygone. Open policy.js in the regular VS Code pane.`



## Return to the intended comparison

Before: release.js was pinned while policy.js was active. The active comparison is Index preview → unsaved nightly. Keep these endpoints while focusing a symbol.

![Return to the intended comparison](images/14b-resume-working.png)

Entry: `Source Control → Changes → release.js → Open Working Changes in Bygone.`



## Choose a symbol from the cursor

Before: the comparison contains the whole file. The selected command uses VS Code’s current cursor or selection. Press Enter to focus this declaration.

![Choose a symbol from the cursor](images/15a-symbol-command.png)

Entry: `Place the cursor inside planRelease. Choose Bygone: Compare Symbol in Bygone.`



## Narrow the view, preserve the comparison

Before: whole-file Index preview → working nightly. Both panes now contain planRelease. The same baseline and live document remain selected.

![Narrow the view, preserve the comparison](images/15-symbol-slice.png)

Entry: `Run Compare Symbol in Bygone from inside planRelease.`



## Edit in Bygone; see it in VS Code

Before: native editor and Bygone both showed nightly. Both now show dev. The index pane still shows preview; this is one shared, unsaved document.

![Edit in Bygone; see it in VS Code](images/16-synced-edit.png)

Entry: `In Bygone’s right-hand symbol pane, replace nightly with dev.`



## Undo once, update both views

Before: the previous edit changed nightly → dev. The regular editor and Bygone both return to nightly. The file is still unsaved.

![Undo once, update both views](images/17-shared-undo.png)

Entry: `Click Undo in Bygone.`



## Save the document, keep the index

Before: working document nightly was dirty; index was preview. Saved buffer replaces Unsaved buffer, and the dirty dot clears. The index remains preview.

![Save the document, keep the index](images/18-save-no-stage.png)

Entry: `Click Save in Bygone.`



## Open a saved review

Before: you were editing a live working document. The review displays its pinned Git identities and cited source references. It is a separate artifact.

![Open a saved review](images/19-evidence-review.png)

Entry: `Run Bygone: Open Evidence Review and select review.json for this repository.`



## Read the exact cited file diff

Before: the review listed a source citation. Bygone opens the review’s committed comparison. Your working nightly text is not substituted into it.

![Read the exact cited file diff](images/21-pinned-diff.png)

Entry: `In Evidence Review, choose Pinned file diff for planRelease.`



## Open a live counterpart for editing

Before: you were inspecting an immutable committed diff. A separate working view opens with Return to Evidence Review available. The live value is nightly.

![Open a live counterpart for editing](images/22-evidence-repair.png)

Entry: `Return to Evidence Review. Choose Edit working counterpart for the same reference.`



## Make a real working edit

Before: the live counterpart showed nightly. The regular document now contains candidate. The captured review still refers to its original commit.

![Make a real working edit](images/22b-working-edit.png)

Entry: `In the regular VS Code pane, replace nightly with candidate. Leave it unsaved.`



## Return to the original evidence

Before: you made an unsaved candidate edit in the working counterpart. The original pinned review is back. The working edit survives separately; no review refresh is implied.

![Return to the original evidence](images/23-return-to-evidence.png)

Entry: `Click Return to Evidence Review.`



## A separate question: file history

The edit-and-return sequence is complete. This starts a different inspection. A dedicated history view opens. Select commits here to investigate how the file evolved.

![A separate question: file history](images/24-vscode-history.png)

Entry: `Optional detour: run Bygone: View Active File History for release.js.`



## Read the argument before the code

An authored tour arranges a change into chapters and scenes. The reading view tells the story; each step can open exact evidence.

![Read the argument before the code](images/25-tour-reader.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo present --tour release.bygone`



## Put a claim beside its evidence

A focused step highlights the relevant source in a pinned comparison. The narrative explains why the change matters, rather than reciting the diff.

![Put a claim beside its evidence](images/26-focused-step.png)

Entry: `Select a step • Show in code`



## Leave the path without losing it

Explore Files or Commits to test the explanation, then return to tour focus. Exploration does not change the authored comparison.

![Leave the path without losing it](images/27-explore-return.png)

Entry: `Files • Commits • Return to tour focus`



## Teach in conceptual stages

Deconstructed tours reorder changes into cumulative explanation stages. The screenshot uses Bygone’s public marker example; these stages are explicitly synthetic, not historical commits.

![Teach in conceptual stages](images/28-deconstructed.png)

Entry: `bygone present --tour examples/deconstructed-diff.bygone`



## Inspect validated symbol correspondence

Strand pairs the edited planRelease declaration across pinned revisions. The tree shows unmatched symbols and analysis limits. Inferred correspondence does not establish behavioral equivalence.

![Inspect validated symbol correspondence](images/31-symbol-tree.png)

Entry: `npm run correspondence:analyze -- feature --base main --engine bygone-strand --output correspondence.json`



## Turn review links into a tour

The real evidence exporter supplies claims and pinned links. The generated tour preserves producer assessments as claims, and explicitly marks verification as not recorded.

![Turn review links into a tour](images/29-evidence-tour.png)

Entry: `bygone -C repo evidence tour imported.json --output evidence.bygone`



## Author an explanation from Git evidence

The authoring surface prepares a prompt grounded in the selected range. Write a .bygone source, validate anchors, and compile before sharing.

![Author an explanation from Git evidence](images/12-authoring.png)

Entry: `bygone tour context feature --base main --output context.json`



## Share a self-contained snapshot

An embedded minimal export opens without a repository or internet runtime. It includes whole referenced file contents, including surrounding and deleted text; review those bytes before sharing.

![Share a self-contained snapshot](images/30-portable.png)

Entry: `bygone tour export release.bygone --output tour.html --profile minimal --runtime embedded`



## Use dependency evidence to widen inspection

A real repair report identifies unchanged direct consumers of the modified module. An unchanged graph is not evidence of unchanged behavior.

![Use dependency evidence to widen inspection](images/32-dependencies.png)

Entry: `bygone evidence inspect review.json --dependencies dependencies.json`

Documentation card derived from actual dependency report; no graph UI is implied.

## Choose a host and entry point

Menus, drag/drop, CLI, deep links, and VS Code commands lead into the same core comparisons. Desktop handoff requires a configured local installation.

![Choose a host and entry point](images/33-hosts.png)

Entry: `bygone --help • bygone completion zsh`

Alternate entry routes are documented, not individually clicked in this capture run.

## Know what the view can prove

Interpret provenance, mutability and fallback labels before editing or drawing conclusions. Snapshot validity, test execution and human approval are separate facts.

![Know what the view can prove](images/34-limits.png)

Untracked and unsupported paths are documented coverage, not additional screenshots/tests in this run.

## Inspect what remains unstaged

Before: the staged comparison was stable → preview. The baseline is now Index preview; the writable side is the saved document canary.

![Inspect what remains unstaged](images/13-scm-working.png)

## Choose active-editor following

![Leave the path without losing it](images/27-explore-return.png)

Entry: `Files • Commits • Return to tour focus`

![Teach in conceptual stages](images/28-deconstructed.png)
